thread:
sara.sales: Hey all — new enterprise POC request. Customer is on Azure, wants Dedicated pool for 2 weeks, 4x A100-ish. They require a single stable egress IP (for firewall allowlisting), VNet peering, and they asked whether we can issue Hosted-style API keys scoped to the Dedicated endpoint. Also pricing estimate for short POC?
pranav.eng: We can allocate a Dedicated pool for a short-term commit. Pricing: typically a 2-week POC gets a pro-rated reserved price + setup fee. I'll ping finance for exact quote but ballpark is monthly pro-rate of the Dedicated SKU.
mike.solutions: For the keys: we don’t issue classic hosted keys to customers for Dedicated — we generate project-scoped API keys that route to their pool. Behavior is the same from app perspective.
kai.network: On networking — Dedicated supports static egress via NAT IPs or a customer-managed NAT in their VNet. For Azure VNet peering we offer private endpoint peering alternative (PrivateLink style). Which do they prefer?
sara.sales: They want the vendor allowlist to contain a single CIDR /32 if possible (security team is strict). Is a single IP guaranteed?
pranav.eng: We can provide a static NAT IP per Dedicated cluster but note: HA and scaling may introduce short rotation windows if they request burstable capacity across multiple AZs. If they require a single /32 with absolute no rotation, we need to lock to a single egress gateway and disable cross-AZ burst — doable for a POC but call it out in the SOW.
kai.network: Also confirm whether the customer’s firewall uses SNI or IP-based allowlist. If they do SNI host checking (some corporate proxies do), our TLS SNI will present the Dedicated host. If they rely on SNI to route, they should allow our hostname(s) too.
mike.solutions: Example allowlist entry we can hand them: 52.149.77.123/32 (sample NAT IP) and hostnames: dedicated.us-east.redwood.example.com. Tell them to allow both IP and SNI host if possible.
sara.sales: Great — legal will also want a note about ephemeral key rotation during the POC. Do keys rotate automatically?
mike.solutions: Keys are long-lived by default but we can issue timeboxed keys for POCs (expires after TTL). For extra security we can recommend short TTL plus IP allowlist.
pranav.eng: From ops side, steps to provision: 1) Sales sends signed POC SOW + billing info. 2) Network team pre-allocates NAT IP and Dedicated pool. 3) We create project and generate scoped API keys. 4) Customer adds allowlist entry. 5) We run smoke tests (embed/stream calls) and share dashboard access.
sara.sales: Can you paste a quick smoke-test curl I can send to customer?
kai.network: Sure:
```
curl -X POST https://dedicated.us-east.redwood.example.com/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"hello"}'
```
pranav.eng: Also mention DNS TTLs — if they allow hostname, their firewall needs to respect DNS changes; for strict single-IP allowlist prefer the static NAT /32.
ops-bot: (provisioning note) created ticket INF-4521 for NAT IP allocation; assigned to kai.network. ETA ~2 business days. :white_check_mark: 
sara.sales: Customer security questionnaire: they asked where TLS terminates. Answer: TLS terminates on our edge for Hosted; for Dedicated with PrivateLink/VNet peering TLS can terminate in customer-managed path — we’ll clarify per deployment. I'll collect exact SOW language.
mike.solutions: One more thing — if they want VNet peering (no public egress), we will set up private endpoint peering and then they must route outbound to our endpoint. That removes need for public NAT IP but requires routing/firewall changes on their side.
sara.sales: Ok, I'll propose two options to the customer: (A) quick POC with static NAT IP /32 + timeboxed keys; (B) secure VNet peering with private endpoint (longer lead, zero public IP). I'll ask which they prefer and get the signed SOW.
kai.network: If they pick option B, request their VNet CIDR + peering contact + preferred BGP (if any). Also confirm any proxy in front of their egress.
sara.sales: Thanks everyone — sending this to the customer now. Will update the thread once they pick option A vs B. :rocket:
